newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms ahead of new reserve rate.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms ahead of new reserve rate.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah continued to strengthen against the dollar in the run-up to the new bank reserve requirement rate on Wednesday, dealers said on Monday.
They said the market was focused on liquidity concerns.

A new reserve rate of five percent will become effective on April 16, up from three percent at present. Dealers were mixed over the possible implications, with some expecting a drain of five to eight trillion rupiah with others seeing little effect.
"I think the impact shouldn't be significant because it has been announced last year," one Japanese bank dealer said, adding that people should have had enough time to prepare.
However, operators were seen focusing on managing their liquidity positions, sending short-term rates up.
Dealers said swap rates rose across the board, possibly due to uncertainty over market conditions after Wednesday.

One European bank dealer said rises in swap rates might be psychological because the reserve rate hike should have equal effect on the dollar and the rupiah, thus keeping interest rate differentials unchanged.
He said some dollar unloading by Singapore players was seen, but spot dollars were supported at the 2,404.0 level.
Spot rupiah was at 2,404.25/04.50 at 0315 GMT against an opening of 2,404.3/05.3. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,403.8/04.00 and 2,403.40/03.85, respectively.
Overnight swap was at 0.45/0.50 and tom/next at 0.47/0.55.
One-month swaps edged up to 13.00/13.75 from 11.75/12.50 on Friday, two to 26.0/27.0 from 24.0/25.0, three to 38.0/38.5 from 34.5/35.5 and six to 73.50/74.25 from 71.0/72.0.
Bank Indonesia kept the intervention band at 2,399/2,591 and the conversion band to 2,399/2,447 on Friday.
